title.zh: 卷154 志一百二十九 邦交二 英吉利
title.raw: 卷154 志一百二十九 邦交二 英吉利

sentences.zh: 英吉利在歐羅巴西北。

translations.literal: Yingjili [England/Britain] lies in the northwest of Europe.
translations.idiomatic: Britain lies in the northwestern part of Europe.

sentences.zh: 清置定海關，英人始來互市，然不能每歲至。

translations.literal: When the Qing established the Dinghai customs, the English first came for mutual trade, yet they could not come every year.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qing set up the Dinghai customs house, the English began to trade, though they could not manage to come every year.

sentences.zh: 來粵東，所載皆黑鉛、番錢、羽緞、哆囉、嗶嘰諸物，未幾去。

translations.literal: When they came to eastern Guangdong, what they carried were black lead, foreign coin, feather satin, woolen broadcloth, baize, and the like; before long they departed.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to eastern Guangdong, their cargoes were lead, foreign silver, feather satin, woolens, baize, and similar goods; they soon sailed away again.

sentences.zh: 七年，始通市不絕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, trade was opened without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, continuous trade was finally established.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，英巡船遭風，飄至廣東澳門，總督策楞令地方官給貲糧、修船舶遣之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh winter month, a British patrol ship met with wind and drifted to Macao in Guangdong; Governor Celen ordered local officials to supply funds and grain, repair the vessel, and send them away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh winter month, a British patrol vessel was caught in a storm and driven to Macao in Guangdong; Governor Celen ordered local officials to provide funds and provisions, repair the ship, and send them on their way.

sentences.zh: 二十年，來寧波互市。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, they came to Ningbo for mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, they came to Ningbo to trade.

sentences.zh: 時英商船收定海港，運貨寧波，逾年遂增數舶。

translations.literal: At the time British merchant ships unloaded at Dinghai harbor and transported goods to Ningbo; after more than a year the number of vessels increased.
translations.idiomatic: British merchant ships then unloaded at Dinghai and carried goods on to Ningbo; within a year several more ships were added.

sentences.zh: 旋禁不許入浙，並禁絲斤出洋。

translations.literal: Shortly they were forbidden to enter Zhejiang, and silk by weight was also forbidden from being exported overseas.
translations.idiomatic: Soon entry into Zhejiang was banned, and the export of raw silk overseas was forbidden as well.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，英商喀喇生、通事洪任輝欲赴寧波開港。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the British merchants Flint and interpreter Hong Rengui wished to go to Ningbo to open a port.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, the British merchant Flint and his interpreter James Flint sought to open trade at Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 既不得請，自海道入天津，仍乞通市寧波，並訐粵海關陋弊。

translations.literal: Having failed to obtain permission, they entered Tianjin by sea, still begging to open trade at Ningbo, and also denounced the corrupt practices of the Guangdong customs.
translations.idiomatic: Denied permission, they sailed to Tianjin, again petitioning for trade at Ningbo while accusing the Guangdong customs of gross abuses.

sentences.zh: 七月，命福州將軍來粵按驗，得其與徽商汪聖儀交結狀，治聖儀罪，而下洪任輝於獄。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Fuzhou general was ordered to come to Guangdong to investigate; evidence was found of his collusion with Huizhou merchant Wang Shengyi; Wang was punished and Hong Rengui was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, the Fuzhou general was sent to Guangdong to investigate; collusion with the Huizhou merchant Wang Shengyi was proved, Wang was punished, and James Flint was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 旋釋之。

translations.literal: Shortly he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was released soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 二十七年夏五月，英商啗㘓等以禁止絲斤，其貨艱于成造，仍求通市。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the twenty-seventh year, British merchants such as Danqin, because silk by weight was forbidden, found their goods hard to manufacture, and still requested trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth summer month of the twenty-seventh year, British merchants including Danqin, finding silk exports banned and their goods hard to finish, again petitioned to trade.

sentences.zh: 粵督蘇昌以聞，許之，然仍限每船隻許配買土絲五千觔，二蠶湖絲三千斤，至頭蠶湖絲及綢緞綾匹仍禁。

translations.literal: Guangdong Governor Su Chang reported it; permission was granted, yet each ship was still limited to purchasing five thousand jin of native silk and three thousand jin of double-cocoon lake silk, while first-cocoon lake silk and satin damask were still forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong Governor Su Chang reported the request and trade was allowed, but each ship might buy only five thousand jin of native silk and three thousand jin of double-cocoon lake silk; first-cocoon lake silk and woven silks remained banned.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，英國王雅治遣使臣馬戛爾尼等來朝貢，表請派人駐京，及通市浙江寧波、珠山、天津、廣東等地，並求減關稅，不許。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, King George of Britain sent envoys such as Macartney to present tribute; the memorial requested resident representatives in the capital, trade at Ningbo in Zhejiang, Zhushan, Tianjin, Guangdong, and other places, and reduced customs duties—all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year, King George III sent Lord Macartney and others on a tribute mission, asking to station envoys in the capital, open trade at Ningbo, Zhushan, Tianjin, Guangdong, and elsewhere, and reduce customs duties; all were denied.

sentences.zh: 六十年，復入貢，表陳「天朝大將軍前年督兵至的密，英國曾發兵應援」。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, tribute was presented again; the memorial stated that "when the Great Qing general led troops to Demi the year before last, Britain had sent troops in support."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year they presented tribute again, stating that when the Qing general had marched on Nepal two years before, Britain had sent troops to assist.

sentences.zh: 的密即廓爾喀也。

translations.literal: Demi is Gurkha [Nepal].
translations.idiomatic: "Demi" here means Gurkha Nepal.

sentences.zh: 奏入，敕書賜賚如例。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; an imperial letter and gifts were bestowed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, an imperial letter and gifts were granted as usual.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏六月，英國遣其臣加拉威禮來粵東投書，言英太子攝政已歷四年，感念純皇帝聖恩，遣使來獻方物，循貢道，由海洋舟山至天津赴都，懇總督先奏。

translations.literal: In the sixth summer month of the twenty-first year, Britain sent its subject Galaweili to Guangdong with a letter, stating that the British crown prince had been regent for four years, mindful of the Pure Emperor's sage grace, and was sending envoys to present local products along the tribute route from Zhoushan by sea to Tianjin to proceed to the capital, earnestly asking the governor-general to memorialize first.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth summer month of the twenty-first year, Britain sent Lord Gower to Guangdong with a letter: the prince regent had ruled four years, mindful of the late emperor's grace, and was dispatching envoys with tribute gifts via Zhoushan and Tianjin to the capital, asking the governor-general to memorialize in advance.

sentences.zh: 時總督蔣攸銛方入朝，巡撫董教增權督篆，許其晉見，援督撫大吏見暹邏諸國貢使禮，加拉威禮不受，再三議相見儀，教增不得已許之。

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General Jiang Yougui had just entered the capital for audience; Governor Dong Jiaozeng acted as governor-general; an audience was permitted, citing the protocol by which governor-generals and governors received tribute envoys from Siam and neighboring states; Galaweili would not accept it; the ceremony of meeting was debated again and again, and Jiaozeng had no choice but to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Jiang Yougui was then in Beijing; Governor Dong Jiaozeng acted in his place and agreed to an audience on the usual terms for receiving Siamese and other tribute missions. Gower refused, haggling repeatedly over ceremony until Jiaozeng reluctantly yielded.

sentences.zh: 其日總督及將軍、兩副都統、海關監督畢坐節堂，陳儀衛，加拉威禮上謁，免冠致敬，通事為達意，教增離坐起立相問答，允為入告，加拉威禮徑出。

translations.literal: On that day the governor-general, the general, the two vice commanders, and the customs superintendent all sat in the hall of ceremony with guards arrayed; Galaweili came forward to pay respects, removed his hat and bowed, the interpreter conveyed his meaning, Jiaozeng rose from his seat to question and answer, agreed to report upward, and Galaweili went straight out.
translations.idiomatic: That day the governor-general, the general, two vice commanders, and the customs superintendent sat in the ceremonial hall with full guard. Gower paid his respects bareheaded; through an interpreter he spoke with Jiaozeng, who rose to reply and promised to report to the court, whereupon Gower withdrew.

sentences.zh: 比教增奏入，而貢使羅爾美都、副貢使馬禮遜乘貢舟五，已達天津。

translations.literal: By the time Jiaozeng's memorial reached the capital, the tribute envoy Lord Amherst and deputy envoy Morrison, riding five tribute ships, had already reached Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jiaozeng's memorial arrived in Beijing, Lord Amherst and Deputy Envoy Morrison had already reached Tianjin with five tribute vessels.

sentences.zh: 帝命戶部尚書和世泰、工部尚書蘇楞額往天津，率長蘆鹽政廣惠伴貢使來京，一日夜馳至圓明園，車路顛簸，又衣裝皆落後。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ministers of Revenue Heshengtai and of Works Suleng'e to go to Tianjin, lead Changlu salt commissioner Guanghui to escort the tribute envoys to the capital, and in one day and night they galloped to the Yuanming Garden; the road was rough and their ceremonial dress had all fallen behind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ministers Heshengtai and Suleng'e to Tianjin to escort the envoys to Beijing with Salt Commissioner Guanghui; they raced to the Yuanming Garden in a day and a night, jolted along bad roads while their court dress lagged behind.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，帝升殿受朝會，時正使已病，副使言衣車未至，無朝服不能成禮，和世泰懼獲譴，詭奏二貢使皆病，遂卻其貢不納，遣廣惠伴押使臣回粵。

translations.literal: At dawn the emperor ascended the hall to receive the audience; the chief envoy was already ill; the deputy said the clothing cart had not arrived and without court dress the rites could not be performed; Heshengtai feared punishment and falsely reported that both tribute envoys were ill; their tribute was therefore refused and Guanghui was sent to escort the envoys back to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor took the audience, but the chief envoy was ill and the deputy said their court dress had not arrived. Fearful of blame, Heshengtai falsely reported both envoys sick; their tribute was refused and Guanghui was sent to escort them back to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 初英貢使齎表，帝覽表文，抗若敵體，又理籓院迓接不如儀，帝故疑其慢，絕不與通。

translations.literal: When the British tribute envoys first presented their memorial, the emperor read the text and found it defiant as toward an equal; moreover the Court of Colonial Affairs had not received them according to protocol; the emperor therefore suspected disrespect and would have no dealings with them.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys first presented their memorial, the emperor found its tone insolently equal and the Court of Colonial Affairs had botched the reception; suspecting deliberate disrespect, he broke off all contact.

sentences.zh: 羅爾美都等既出都，有以實入告者，帝始知非貢使罪，復降諭錫賚，追及良鄉，酌收貢物，仍賜國王珍玩數事，並敕諭國王歸咎使臣不遵禮節謝宴，英使怏怏去。

translations.literal: After Lord Amherst and the others had left the capital, someone reported the true facts; the emperor then knew it was not the envoys' fault; he again issued edicts and gifts, overtook them at Liangxiang, accepted part of the tribute, still bestowed several precious objects on the king, and instructed the king to blame the envoys for not observing ritual and declining the banquet; the English envoys departed resentfully.
translations.idiomatic: After the envoys left Beijing, the truth reached the emperor; he sent gifts after them as far as Liangxiang, accepted part of the tribute, and sent curios to the king with orders to blame the envoys for breach of ceremony. The British mission withdrew in ill humor.

sentences.zh: 七月，降革蘇楞額、和世泰、廣惠等有差。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Suleng'e, Heshengtai, Guanghui, and others were demoted and punished to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Suleng'e, Heshengtai, Guanghui, and others were demoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 十六年，定食鴉片煙罪。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, penalties for consuming opium were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, penalties for smoking opium were established.

sentences.zh: 初，英自以後，私設貯煙大舶十餘隻，謂之「躉船」，又省城包買戶，謂之「窯口」。

translations.literal: At first, from this time onward, the English privately set up more than ten large ships for storing opium, called "receiver ships," and in the provincial capital there were purchasing agents called "kiln mouths."
translations.idiomatic: From this time the English privately maintained a dozen or more opium storage ships called "receiver ships," and wholesale buyers in the provincial capital known as "kiln mouths."

sentences.zh: 由窯口兌價銀於英館，由英館給票單至躉船取貨。

translations.literal: Through the kiln mouths silver was exchanged at the English factory; the factory issued tickets to take goods from the receiver ships.
translations.idiomatic: Kiln mouths paid silver at the English factory, which issued receipts for collection from the receiver ships.

sentences.zh: 有來往護艇，名曰「快蟹」，砲械畢具。

translations.literal: There were escort boats going back and forth, called "fast crabs," fully equipped with cannon and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Armed escort boats called "fast crabs" shuttled back and forth, fully mounted with guns.

sentences.zh: 太常寺卿許乃濟見銀輸出歲千餘萬，奏請弛煙禁，令英商仍照藥材納稅，入關交行後，只許以貨易貨，不得用銀購買，以示限制。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices official Xu Naiji, seeing more than ten million taels of silver exported yearly, memorialized to relax the opium ban, ordering English merchants still to pay tax as on medicinals; after entering customs and handing goods to brokers, only barter for goods was permitted, not purchase with silver, to show restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Naiji of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, noting annual silver exports above ten million taels, urged relaxing the ban: opium should be taxed as medicine, traded only by barter after entry, and not bought with silver as a check on outflow.

sentences.zh: 已報可，旋因疆臣奏請嚴販賣吸食罪名，加重至死，而私販私吸如故。

translations.literal: Approval was already granted; shortly afterward frontier officials memorialized to tighten penalties for selling and consuming, increasing them up to death, yet private sale and private consumption continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Approval had been granted, but frontier officials soon demanded harsher penalties up to death for sale and use; smuggling and smoking continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十八年，鴻臚寺卿黃爵滋請嚴吸食罪，行保甲連坐之法，且謂其禍烈於洪水猛獸。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Court of State Ceremonial official Huang Juezi requested strict penalties for consumption, implementing collective punishment through the baojia system, and said its harm was fiercer than flood and wild beasts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Huang Juezi of the Court of State Ceremonial urged severe penalties for smokers with baojia collective responsibility, declaring the harm worse than flood or wild beasts.

sentences.zh: 疏上，下各督撫議，於是請禁者紛起。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; it was sent down to each governor and governor-general for discussion; then petitions to ban proliferated.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up and was referred to every province; memorials calling for prohibition multiplied.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督林則徐奏尤剴切，言：「鴉片不禁絕，則國日貧，民日弱，十餘年後，豈惟無可籌之餉，抑且無可用之兵。」

translations.literal: Huguang Governor-General Lin Zexu memorialized most earnestly, saying: "If opium is not utterly prohibited, the state grows poorer day by day and the people weaker day by day; after more than ten years, not only will there be no funds to raise, but there will be no usable troops."
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Governor-General Lin Zexu wrote with especial force: "Unless opium is utterly banned, the state grows poorer and the people weaker daily; within a decade there will be neither revenue to levy nor soldiers fit to fight."

sentences.zh: 帝深然其言，詔至京面授方略，以兵部尚書頒欽差大臣關防，赴粵東查辦。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved his words, ordered him to the capital to receive strategy in person, and as Minister of War issued the imperial commissioner seal to go to Guangdong to investigate and handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed, summoned him to Beijing, and as Minister of War commissioned him with the imperial commissioner's seal to investigate in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 明年春正月，至粵東，與總督鄧廷楨會申煙禁，頒新律：以一年又六月為限，吸煙罪絞，販煙罪斬。

translations.literal: In the first spring month of the following year he reached Guangdong, joined Governor-General Deng Tingzhen in proclaiming the opium ban, and promulgated new statutes: within one year and six months as the limit, smoking was punishable by strangulation and trafficking by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he reached Guangdong, joined Deng Tingzhen in enforcing the ban, and issued new law: smokers faced strangulation and traffickers decapitation after eighteen months' grace.

sentences.zh: 時嚴捕煙犯，洋人泊零丁洋諸躉船將徙避，則徐咨水師提督各營分路扼守，令在洋躉船先繳煙方許開艙。

translations.literal: At the time opium offenders were strictly arrested; foreigners anchored receiver ships at Lintin and elsewhere intending to move away to avoid capture; Lin consulted the naval commander to have each camp block routes separately, ordering receiver ships at sea to surrender opium first before opening cargo holds.
translations.idiomatic: As arrests intensified, foreign receiver ships at Lintin prepared to flee; Lin ordered the navy to block every route and required opium surrendered before any ship might open its holds.

sentences.zh: 又傳集十三行商人等，令諭各商估煙土存儲實數，並索歷年販煙之查頓、顛地二人，查頓遁走。

translations.literal: He also summoned the Thirteen Hong merchants and others, ordering them to inform each merchant of the actual amount of opium stored, and also demanded the two men Dent and Jardine who had trafficked opium for years; Dent fled.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the Thirteen Hong merchants to report stored opium and demanded Dent and Jardine, long-time traffickers; Dent escaped.

sentences.zh: 義律託故回澳門。

translations.literal: Elliot pleaded an excuse and returned to Macao.
translations.idiomatic: Charles Elliot pleaded business and withdrew to Macao.

sentences.zh: 及事亟，斷水陸餉道，義律乃使各商繳所存煙土，凡二萬二百八十三箱，則徐命悉焚之，而每箱償以茶葉五斤，復令各商具「永不售賣煙土」結。

translations.literal: When the affair grew urgent, water and land supply routes were cut off; Elliot then had each merchant surrender stored opium, altogether 20,283 chests; Lin ordered all burned, compensating five jin of tea per chest, and again ordered each merchant to submit a bond "never to sell opium."
translations.idiomatic: As pressure mounted Lin cut supplies by land and sea; Elliot then had merchants surrender 20,283 chests, which Lin burned, paying five jin of tea per chest and requiring bonds never to deal in opium again.

sentences.zh: 於是煙商失利，遂生觖望。

translations.literal: Thereupon the opium merchants suffered loss and resentment arose.
translations.idiomatic: The opium traders suffered heavy losses and resentment grew.

sentences.zh: 義律恥見挫辱，乃鼓動國人，冀國王出干預。

translations.literal: Elliot, ashamed at being humiliated, stirred his countrymen, hoping the king would intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Elliot roused his compatriots and hoped the king would intervene.

sentences.zh: 國王謀於上下議院，僉以此類貿易本干中國例禁，其曲在我。

translations.literal: The king consulted the upper and lower houses of Parliament; all agreed that this sort of trade violated China's standing prohibitions and the fault lay on their side.
translations.idiomatic: The king consulted Parliament; both houses agreed the trade violated Chinese law and Britain was in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 遂有律土丹者，上書求禁，並請禁印度栽種。

translations.literal: Thereupon one Lüshidan memorialized seeking prohibition, and also asked to ban cultivation in India.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shaftesbury then petitioned for prohibition and an end to cultivation in India.

sentences.zh: 又有地爾窪，作鴉片罪過論，以為既壞中國風俗，又使中國猜忌英人，反礙商務。

translations.literal: There was also Dierwa, who wrote a treatise on the crimes of opium, holding that it both corrupted Chinese customs and made China suspicious of the English, actually hindering commerce.
translations.idiomatic: Dwarkanath Tagore wrote on opium's evils: it corrupted Chinese morals, bred suspicion of Britain, and harmed legitimate trade.

sentences.zh: 然自燒煙之信傳入外洋，茶絲日見翔踴，銀利日長，義律遂以為鴉片興衰，實關民生國計。

translations.literal: Yet since news of burning the opium spread overseas, tea and silk prices rose daily and silver profits grew daily; Elliot therefore held that the rise and fall of opium truly concerned the people's livelihood and the state's finances.
translations.idiomatic: But when news of the burning reached abroad, tea and silk prices soared and silver profits grew; Elliot concluded opium's fate was a matter of national prosperity.

sentences.zh: 時林則徐令各洋船先停洋面候查，必無攜帶鴉片者，始許入口開艙。

translations.literal: At the time Lin Zexu ordered each foreign ship first to anchor on the outer sea awaiting inspection; only those certainly not carrying opium were permitted to enter and open holds.
translations.idiomatic: Lin ordered every foreign ship to anchor offshore for inspection; only vessels proved opium-free might enter and unload.

sentences.zh: 各國商俱如命。

translations.literal: Merchants of every nation all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants of every nation complied.

sentences.zh: 獨義律抗不遵命，謂必俟其國王命定章程，方許貨船入口，而遞書請許其國貨船泊近澳門，不入黃埔。

translations.literal: Only Elliot resisted and would not obey, saying cargo ships could enter only after his king ordered regulations fixed, and sent letters requesting that his nation's cargo ships be allowed to anchor near Macao and not enter Whampoa.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot alone refused, insisting entry await royal instructions, and asked that British ships anchor near Macao instead of Whampoa.

sentences.zh: 則徐嚴駁不許，又禁絕薪蔬食物入澳。

translations.literal: Lin sternly rejected and forbade it, and also cut off fuel, vegetables, and food entering Macao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin rejected the request and cut off provisions to Macao.

sentences.zh: 義律率妻子去澳，寄居尖沙嘴貨船，乃潛招其國兵船二，又取貨船配以砲械，假索食，突攻九龍山。

translations.literal: Elliot led his wife and children out of Macao, lodged on a cargo ship at Kowloon Point, secretly summoned two of his nation's warships, also took cargo ships and fitted them with cannon and arms, feigned seeking food, and suddenly attacked Kowloon Hill.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot moved his family from Macao to a merchant ship at Kowloon, secretly summoned two warships, armed cargo vessels, and under pretense of seeking food attacked Kowloon Hill.

sentences.zh: 參將賴恩爵砲沈其雙桅船一，餘船留漢仔者亦為水師攻毀。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander Lai Enjue sank one of their brigantines with cannon; remaining ships left at Hankou were also attacked and destroyed by the navy.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander Lai Enjue sank one brig with gunfire; the navy destroyed the rest at Hankou.

sentences.zh: 義律求澳人轉圜，原遵新例，惟不肯即交毆斃村民之犯；

translations.literal: Elliot asked Macao people to mediate, originally willing to follow the new regulations, only refusing immediately to hand over the criminals who had beaten villagers to death;
translations.idiomatic: Elliot asked Macao intermediaries to mediate, agreeing to obey the new rules but refusing to surrender the men who had killed villagers;

sentences.zh: 又上書請毋逐尖沙嘴貨船，且俟其國王之命。

translations.literal: he also sent a letter asking not to expel the cargo ships at Kowloon Point, and to await his king's command.
translations.idiomatic: he also wrote asking that ships at Kowloon not be expelled and that action await orders from London.

sentences.zh: 水師提督關天培以不交犯，擲還其書。

translations.literal: Naval Commander Guan Tianpei, because the criminals were not surrendered, threw back his letter.
translations.idiomatic: Naval Commander Guan Tianpei returned the letter unread because the culprits were not handed over.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，天培擊敗英人，義律遁。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, Tianpei defeated the English and Elliot fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Guan Tianpei routed the British and Elliot fled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，罷英人互市，英貨船三十餘艘皆不得入。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, English mutual trade was suspended; more than thirty English cargo ships were all forbidden entry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month British trade was suspended and more than thirty British merchantmen were barred from port.

sentences.zh: 又搜捕偵探船，日數起。

translations.literal: Spy ships were also hunted and seized, several cases daily.
translations.idiomatic: Spy boats were hunted down in several captures a day.

sentences.zh: 英商人人怨義律，義律不得已，復遣人投書乞恩，請仍回居澳門。

translations.literal: Every English merchant resented Elliot; Elliot had no choice and again sent someone with a letter begging favor, asking still to return to dwell in Macao.
translations.idiomatic: British merchants blamed Elliot; he sent another plea begging to be allowed back to Macao.

sentences.zh: 林則徐以新奉旨難驟更，復嚴斥與之絕。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu, because he had newly received an imperial order and could not suddenly change, again sternly rebuked and broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, bound by fresh imperial orders, rebuked him again and broke off contact.

sentences.zh: 而英貨船皆泊老萬山外洋不肯去，惟以厚利啗島濱亡命漁舟蜑艇致薪蔬，且以鴉片與之市。

translations.literal: Yet English cargo ships all anchored on the outer sea off Lao Wan Shan and would not leave, only using rich profit to entice island shore desperadoes, fishing boats, and Tanka craft to bring fuel and vegetables, and also traded opium with them.
translations.idiomatic: British ships lingered off Lao Wan Shan, bribing fishermen and Tanka boats for provisions while trading opium on the side.

sentences.zh: 是月，廣東增嚴海防。

translations.literal: That month, Guangdong tightened coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: That month Guangdong strengthened coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 二十年春正月，廣東遊擊班格爾馬辛焚運煙濟英匪船二十餘。

translations.literal: In the first spring month of the twentieth year, Guangdong Commander Banger Maxin burned more than twenty ships carrying opium to aid English bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first spring month of the twentieth year Commander Banger Maxin burned more than twenty opium supply ships bound for the British.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，林則徐復遣兵逐英人於磨刀洋。

translations.literal: In the fifth summer month, Lin Zexu again sent troops to drive the English from Modaomen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth summer month Lin again sent troops to drive the British from Modaomen.

sentences.zh: 時義律先回國請益兵，其國遂命伯麥率兵船十餘及印度兵船二十餘來粵，泊金星門。

translations.literal: At the time Elliot had first returned home to request more troops; his country then ordered Bremer to lead more than ten warships and more than twenty Indian warships to Guangdong, anchoring at Golden Star Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot had returned home for reinforcements; Britain sent Bremer with a dozen warships and twenty Indian vessels to Guangdong, anchoring at Golden Star Gate.

sentences.zh: 則徐以火艘乘風潮往攻，英船避去。

translations.literal: Lin used fire ships riding wind and tide to attack; English ships avoided and left.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sent fire ships downwind to attack; the British squadron slipped away.

sentences.zh: 英人見粵防嚴，謀擾閩，敗於廈門。

translations.literal: The English, seeing Guangdong's defense strict, plotted to harass Fujian and were defeated at Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Guangdong too strong, the British turned on Fujian and were beaten at Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 六月，攻定海，殺知縣姚懷祥等。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they attacked Dinghai and killed Magistrate Yao Huaixiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they took Dinghai and killed Magistrate Yao Huaixiang and others.

sentences.zh: 事聞，特旨命兩江總督伊里布為欽差大臣，赴浙督師。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, a special edict appointed Liangjiang Governor-General Yilibu as imperial commissioner to go to Zhejiang to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: On report of the disaster, Yilibu, governor-general of Liangjiang, was appointed imperial commissioner to command in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 七月，則徐遣副將陳連升、遊擊班格爾馬辛，率船五艘攻英帥士密於磨刀洋。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Lin sent Vice Commander Chen Liansheng and Commander Banger Maxin, leading five ships to attack English commander Smith at Modaomen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Lin sent Chen Liansheng and Banger Maxin with five ships against Admiral Smith at Modaomen.

sentences.zh: 班格爾馬辛一艘先至，乘風攻之，砲破其船。

translations.literal: Banger Maxin's one ship arrived first, attacked riding the wind, and cannon breached their ship.
translations.idiomatic: Banger Maxin's lead ship closed under wind and shot Smith's vessel to pieces.

sentences.zh: 八月，義律來天津要撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Elliot came to Tianjin seeking pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Elliot came to Tianjin demanding peace talks.

sentences.zh: 時大學士琦善任直隸總督，義律以其國巴里滿衙門照會中國宰相書，遣人詣大沽口上之，多所要索：一，索貨價；

translations.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Qishan served as Zhili governor-general; Elliot, with his nation's Parliament office note to China's prime minister, sent someone to present it at Dagu mouth, with many demands: first, demand payment for goods;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Qishan was then Zhili governor-general; Elliot sent Parliament's note to the Chinese premier at Dagu with many demands: first, indemnity for seized goods;

sentences.zh: 二，索廣州、廈門、福州、定海各港口為市埠；

translations.literal: second, demand Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, and Dinghai ports as trading marts;
translations.idiomatic: second, trading ports at Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, and Dinghai;

sentences.zh: 三，欲敵體平行；

translations.literal: third, wish for equal standing as between equals;
translations.idiomatic: third, diplomatic equality;

sentences.zh: 四，索犒軍費；

translations.literal: fourth, demand military consolation funds;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, war expenses;

sentences.zh: 五，不得以外洋販煙之船貽累岸商；

translations.literal: fifth, that ships trafficking opium on the outer sea must not implicate shore merchants;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, that shore merchants not be liable for opium ships at sea;

sentences.zh: 六，欲盡裁洋商浮費。

translations.literal: sixth, wish to abolish entirely the incidental fees of foreign merchants.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, abolition of all customary fees on foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 琦善力持撫議，旋宴其酋目二十餘人，許陳奏。

translations.literal: Qishan strongly upheld pacification talks, soon feasted more than twenty of their chiefs and officers, and permitted them to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan pressed for negotiation, entertained twenty British officers, and promised to memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 遂入都面陳撫事。

translations.literal: He then entered the capital to report the pacification affair in person.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Beijing to report in person.

sentences.zh: 乃頒欽差大臣關防，命琦善赴粵東查辦。

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial commissioner seal was issued and Qishan was ordered to go to Guangdong to investigate and handle matters.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial commissioner's seal was issued and Qishan was sent to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 是月，免浙江巡撫烏爾恭額，以失守海疆，又英人投書不受故也。

translations.literal: That month, Zhejiang Governor Wuerhong'e was dismissed for losing the coastal frontier, and also because he would not receive English letters.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhejiang Governor Wuerhong'e was dismissed for losing the coast and refusing British correspondence.

sentences.zh: 義律既起椗，過山東，巡撫託渾布具犒迎送，代義律奏事，謂義律恭順，且感皇上派欽差赴粵查辦恩。

translations.literal: After Elliot set sail, passing Shandong, Governor Tuohunbu prepared consolation gifts to welcome and send him off, memorializing on Elliot's behalf, saying Elliot was respectful and submissive and also grateful for the emperor's grace in dispatching an imperial commissioner to Guangdong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Sailing south Elliot passed Shandong; Governor Tuohunbu entertained him and memorialized that Elliot was submissive and grateful for the imperial commissioner sent to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 罷兩廣總督林則徐，上諭切責，以怡良暫署總督事。

translations.literal: Liangguang Governor-General Lin Zexu was dismissed; an imperial edict sharply rebuked him; Yiliang temporarily acted as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu was dismissed from the Liangguang post with a sharp imperial rebuke; Yiliang acted temporarily as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 會義律南行過蘇，復潛赴鎮海。

translations.literal: As Elliot traveled south passing Suzhou, he again secretly went to Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot sailed south past Suzhou but secretly made for Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 時伊里布駐浙，接琦善議撫咨，遣家丁張喜赴英船犒師。

translations.literal: At the time Yilibu was stationed in Zhejiang; receiving Qishan's pacification consultation, he sent household retainer Zhang Xi to the English ships to present consolation gifts to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yilibu in Zhejiang, on Qishan's word of peace talks, sent his servant Zhang Xi with gifts to the British fleet.

sentences.zh: 英水師統領伯麥踞定海數月，聞撫事定，聽洋艘四出遊弈。

translations.literal: English naval commander Bremer had occupied Dinghai for months; hearing pacification was settled, he allowed foreign ships to roam in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Bremer had held Dinghai for months; hearing peace was agreed, he let his squadron cruise freely.

sentences.zh: 至餘姚，有土人誘其五桅船入攔淺灘，獲黑白洋人數十。

translations.literal: Reaching Yuyao, local people lured their five-masted ship into a shallow bar and captured several dozen white and black foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: Off Yuyao locals lured a five-masted ship aground and captured dozens of British sailors.

sentences.zh: 伊里布聞之，飛檄餘姚縣設供張，委員護入粵。

translations.literal: When Yilibu heard, he urgently dispatched a message to Yuyao county to prepare supplies and entertainment, and appointed officials to escort them into Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yilibu hurriedly ordered Yuyao to entertain them and sent escorts to conduct them to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，琦善抵廣州，尋授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, Qishan reached Guangzhou and soon was appointed Liangguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Qishan reached Guangzhou and was soon made governor-general of Liangguang.

sentences.zh: 義律請撤沿海諸防。

translations.literal: Elliot requested withdrawal of all coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot asked that coastal defenses be dismantled.

sentences.zh: 虎門為廣州水道咽喉，水師提督駐焉。

translations.literal: Humen was the throat of Guangzhou's water route; the naval commander was stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Humen guarded the approach to Guangzhou, where the naval commander was posted.

sentences.zh: 其外大角、沙角二砲臺，燒煙後，益增戍守。

translations.literal: Outside it were the two batteries Dajiao and Shajiao; after burning the opium, garrison defense was further increased.
translations.idiomatic: The outer batteries at Dajiao and Shajiao had been reinforced after the opium burning.

sentences.zh: 師船、火船及蜑艇、扒龍、快蟹，悉列口門內外，密佈橫檔暗椿，至是裁撤殆盡。

translations.literal: War ships, fire ships, and Tanka craft, dragon scrapers, and fast crabs were all arrayed inside and outside the mouth; hidden stakes were densely laid across the channel—by this time they were cut back almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: War junks, fire ships, Tanka craft, and escort boats had lined the channel with hidden stakes; now nearly all were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 義律遂日夜增船櫓，造攻具；

translations.literal: Elliot then day and night increased ships and oars and made assault equipment;
translations.idiomatic: Elliot meanwhile built up his fleet and siege gear night and day;

sentences.zh: 首索煙價，繼求香港，且行文趣琦善速覆。

translations.literal: first demanding opium payment, then seeking Hong Kong, and also sending documents urging Qishan to reply quickly.
translations.idiomatic: first demanding opium indemnity, then Hong Kong, while pressing Qishan for a quick answer.

sentences.zh: 十二月五日，突攻沙角砲臺，副將陳連升等兵不能支，遂陷，皆死之。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the twelfth month, they suddenly attacked Shajiao battery; Vice Commander Chen Liansheng and others' troops could not hold and it fell; all died.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of the twelfth month they stormed Shajiao Fort; Chen Liansheng's men could not hold and all perished when it fell.

sentences.zh: 英人又以火輪、三板赴三門口，焚我戰船十數艘，水師亦潰。

translations.literal: The English also used steamers and longboats to go to Sanmenkou, burned more than ten of our war ships, and the navy also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Steamers and longboats then entered Sanmenkou, burned a dozen Chinese warships, and the fleet broke.

sentences.zh: 英人乘勝攻大角砲臺，千總黎志安受傷，推砲落水，潰圍出，砲臺陷。

translations.literal: The English, riding victory, attacked the Tayou battery; Company Officer Li Zhi'an was wounded, pushed cannon into the water, broke out of the encirclement, and the battery fell.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing their advantage, British forces stormed the Tayou battery. Company Officer Li Zhi'an was wounded; his men tipped guns into the water as they fought out of the encirclement, but the fort was lost.

sentences.zh: 英人悉取水中砲，分兵戍守，於是虎門危急。

translations.literal: The English entirely took the cannon in the water, divided troops to garrison and guard, and thus Humen became critically perilous.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered every gun from the water, posted detachments to hold the positions, and the situation at Humen turned critical.

sentences.zh: 水師提督關天培、總兵李廷鈺、遊擊班格爾馬辛等守靖遠、威遠砲臺，僅兵數百，遣弁告急，不應。

translations.literal: Naval Commander Guan Tianpei, Regional Commander Li Tingyu, and Mobile Corps Commander Ban Ge'er Maxin and others defended the Jingyuan and Weiyuan batteries with only several hundred soldiers; they dispatched sub-officers to report urgency, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Naval commander Guan Tianpei, regional commander Li Tingyu, Mobile Corps Commander Ban Ge'er Maxin, and others held the Jingyuan and Weiyuan forts with only a few hundred men. Repeated urgent appeals through subordinates went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 廷鈺至省泣求增兵，以固省城門戶。

translations.literal: Tingyu arrived at the province and, weeping, begged for added troops to solidify the provincial capital's gate and portal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingyu came to the provincial seat in tears, pleading for reinforcements to shore up the capital's outer defenses.

sentences.zh: 琦善恐妨撫議，不許。

translations.literal: Qishan feared it would obstruct the pacification discussions and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan, fearing reinforcements would derail peace talks, refused.

sentences.zh: 文武僚屬皆力請，始允遣兵五百。

translations.literal: Civil and military subordinates all forcefully requested, and only then was sending five hundred troops permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the entire civil and military staff pressed the point did he agree to send five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 義律仍挾兵力索煙價及香港。

translations.literal: Elliot still relied on military force to demand opium indemnity and Hong Kong.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot continued to use military pressure to demand both an opium indemnity and the cession of Hong Kong.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春正月，琦善以香港許英，而未敢入奏，乃歸浙江英俘易定海。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-first year, Qishan granted Hong Kong to the British but did not dare enter a memorial; he then returned British captives from Zhejiang to exchange for Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, year 21 of the Daoguang reign, Qishan secretly promised Hong Kong to Britain without daring to report it to the throne. Instead he returned British prisoners captured in Zhejiang in exchange for the recovery of Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 義律先遣人赴浙繳還定海，續請獻沙角、大角砲臺以易之。

translations.literal: Elliot first sent men to Zhejiang to hand back Dinghai, then further requested offering the Shajiao and Tayou batteries in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot first sent envoys to Zhejiang to hand back Dinghai, then asked that the Shajiao and Tayou forts be surrendered in return.

sentences.zh: 琦善與訂期會於蓮花城。

translations.literal: Qishan with him fixed a date to meet at Lianhua City.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan and Elliot set a date to meet at Lianhua City.

sentences.zh: 義律出所定貿易章程，並給予香港全島，如澳門故事，皆私許之。

translations.literal: Elliot produced the fixed trade regulations and also granted the whole island of Hong Kong, like the Macao precedent—all privately permitted by him.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot presented his drafted commercial regulations and handed over all of Hong Kong Island on the Macao model—all concessions Qishan made on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 既而琦善以義律來文入奏，帝怒不許。

translations.literal: Subsequently Qishan memorialized the Emperor with Elliot's incoming document; the Emperor was angry and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Qishan finally submitted Elliot's letter to the court, the Emperor was furious and rejected the terms.

sentences.zh: 罷琦善並伊里布，命宗室奕山為靖逆將軍，尚書隆文、湖南提督楊芳為參贊大臣，赴粵剿辦。

translations.literal: Qishan and Yilibu were dismissed; the clansman Yishan was ordered as Pacification-General, Ministers Long Wen and Hunan Provincial Commander Yang Fang as Advisory Grand Ministers, going to Guangdong to suppress and handle.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan and Yilibu were removed from office. The imperial clansman Yishan was appointed Pacification General, with Long Wen, a minister of state, and Yang Fang, Hunan provincial military commander, as grand commissioners to prosecute the war in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時義律以香港已經琦善允給，遍諭居民，以香港為英屬埠。

translations.literal: At the time Elliot, because Hong Kong had already been permitted and given by Qishan, broadly announced to residents, taking Hong Kong as a British-subject port.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Elliot proclaimed throughout Hong Kong that Qishan's pledge made it a British possession.

sentences.zh: 又牒大鵬營副將令撤營汛。

translations.literal: Again he sent a document to the Deputy Regional Commander of Dapeng Camp ordering withdrawal of camp garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a formal notice to the Dapeng deputy commander ordering the removal of frontier garrison posts.

sentences.zh: 粵撫怡良聞之，大駭，奏聞。

translations.literal: Guangdong Governor Yiliang heard this, was greatly alarmed, and memorialized to inform.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong governor Yiliang learned of this, he was horrified and immediately reported it to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，合籍琦善家。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angry and confiscated the registers of Qishan's household by decree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and ordered the confiscation of all of Qishan's property.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔暴英人罪，促奕山等兼程進，會各路官兵進剿。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued exposing British crimes, urging Yishan and others to advance by doubled stages, assembling officers and soldiers on every route to advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then promulgated denouncing British crimes and ordering Yishan and the other commanders to hurry south while troops on every front moved to attack.

sentences.zh: 尋以兩江總督裕謙為欽差大臣，赴浙視師。

translations.literal: Soon the Two-Jiangs Governor-General Yu Qian was made Imperial Commissioner, going to Zhejiang to inspect the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, governor-general of Jiangsu and Jiangxi, was shortly afterward appointed imperial commissioner to take command in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時定海、鎮海等處英船四出遊弈，裕謙遣兵節次焚剿，並誅其酋目一人。

translations.literal: At the time at Dinghai, Zhenhai, and other places British ships went out in all directions on patrol; Yu Qian dispatched troops in sequence to burn and suppress, and also executed one of their chieftain-officers.
translations.idiomatic: British vessels were then ranging from Dinghai to Zhenhai and beyond. Yu Qian sent troops in successive operations to burn and harry them, and put one British officer to death.

sentences.zh: 二月，英人犯虎門，水師提督關天培死之；

translations.literal: In the second month, the British violated Humen; Naval Commander Guan Tianpei died therein;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the British assaulted Humen, and naval commander Guan Tianpei was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 乘勝薄烏湧，省城大震。

translations.literal: Riding victory they pressed close to Wuyong; the provincial city was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious, they pressed on toward Wuyong, throwing the provincial capital into panic.

sentences.zh: 十三日，參贊楊芳抵粵，各路官兵未集，而虎門內外舟師悉被毀。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day, Advisory Minister Yang Fang arrived at Guangdong; troops from all routes were not yet gathered, while inside and outside Humen the boat armies were entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth Yang Fang reached Canton, but the relief armies had not yet assembled and the entire fleet at Humen had already been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 楊芳議以堵為剿，使總兵段永福率千兵扼守東勝寺，陸路總兵長春率千兵扼鳳凰岡水路。

translations.literal: Yang Fang discussed using blocking as suppression, causing Regional Commander Duan Yongfu to lead a thousand troops to hold and guard Dongsheng Temple, and Land-route Regional Commander Changchun to lead a thousand troops to hold the Fenghuang Gang water route.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang decided on a strategy of containment, posting Regional Commander Duan Yongfu with a thousand men at Dongsheng Temple and land-route commander Changchun with a thousand at the Fenghuang Gang waterway.

sentences.zh: 英人率師近逼，雖經鳳凰岡官兵擊退，仍乘潮深入，飛砲火箭並力注攻。

translations.literal: The British led armies to press close; although they were beaten back by Fenghuang Gang officers and soldiers, they still rode the tide to penetrate deeply, flying cannon and fire-arrows together exerting force in focused attack.
translations.idiomatic: British columns closed in. They were briefly driven back at Fenghuang Gang, but then exploited the rising tide to push upstream under concentrated barrages of artillery and rockets.

sentences.zh: 會美領事以戰事礙各國商船進口，赴營請進埔開艙，兼為英人說和，謂英人繳還定海，惟求通商如舊，並出義律書，有「惟求照常貿易，如帶違禁物，即將貨船入官」之文。

translations.literal: It happened that the American consul, because warfare obstructed the various nations' merchant ships entering port, went to camp requesting entry to Huangpu to open warehouses, and also mediated peace for the British, saying the British would return Dinghai, only seeking trade as before, and produced Elliot's letter with the text "only seek to trade as usual; if bringing prohibited goods, then the cargo ships will be confiscated by the government."
translations.idiomatic: The American consul intervened, arguing that fighting was blocking merchant shipping. He asked that Huangpu be opened for trade and offered to mediate, claiming the British would restore Dinghai in return for trade on the old terms. He showed a letter from Elliot stating that Britain wanted only normal commerce and would accept confiscation of any cargo carrying contraband.

sentences.zh: 時定海師船亦至粵，楊芳欲藉此緩兵退敵，遂與怡良聯銜奏請。

translations.literal: At the time Dinghai warships also arrived at Guangdong; Yang Fang wished to borrow this to ease troops and repel the enemy, and then with Yiliang jointly signed a memorial requesting.
translations.idiomatic: A British squadron from Dinghai had also reached Canton. Hoping to use the mediation to gain time, Yang Fang joined Yiliang in a joint memorial asking permission to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 帝以其復踵請撫故轍，嚴旨切責不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because they again followed the old track of requesting pacification, with stern edict sharply rebuked and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw this as the same old appeasement playbook and issued a stern rebuke refusing any negotiation.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔林則徐會辦浙江軍務，尋復遣戍新疆。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict ordered Lin Zexu to jointly handle Zhejiang military affairs; soon after he was again banished to service in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Lin Zexu was recalled to assist with military affairs in Zhejiang, only to be exiled to Xinjiang again soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 四月，奕山以楊芳、隆文等軍分路夜襲英人，不克。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Yishan with Yang Fang, Long Wen, and others' armies divided routes in night assault on the British, not succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yishan launched a coordinated night assault with Yang Fang, Long Wen, and other columns. It failed.

sentences.zh: 英人遂犯廣州城。

translations.literal: The British then violated Guangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: The British then pressed the attack on Canton itself.

sentences.zh: 不得已，仍議款。

translations.literal: Having no alternative, they still discussed terms.
translations.idiomatic: With no other choice, the Chinese side reopened negotiations.

sentences.zh: 義律索煙價千二百萬。

translations.literal: Elliot demanded opium indemnity of twelve million.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot demanded twelve million taels as opium indemnity.

sentences.zh: 美商居間，許其半。

translations.literal: American merchants mediated between, and half was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: American merchants brokered the talks, and the Chinese agreed to pay half.

sentences.zh: 議既定，奕山奏稱義律乞撫，求許照舊通商，永不售賣鴉片，將所償費六百萬改為追交商欠。

translations.literal: Once discussions were settled, Yishan memorialized stating Elliot begged pacification, requesting permission to trade as before, never to sell opium again, changing the compensated fee of six million to pursuit and payment of merchants' debts.
translations.idiomatic: When terms were settled Yishan reported that Elliot had sued for peace, asked to resume trade under the old rules, pledged never again to deal in opium, and reframed the six million indemnity as recovery of debts owed to merchants.

sentences.zh: 撫議既定，英人以撤四方砲臺兵將擾佛山鎮，取道泥城，經蕭關、三元里，里民憤起，號召各鄉壯勇，四面邀截，英兵死者二百餘，殪其渠帥伯麥等。

translations.literal: Once pacification discussions were settled, the British, withdrawing troops from batteries in all four directions, would disturb Foshan town, taking the route through Nicheng, passing Xiaoguan and Sanyuanli; village residents angrily rose, calling forth braves from each township, intercepting on four sides; more than two hundred British soldiers died, and their leader-commander Bremer and others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the truce was agreed, British units withdrawing garrisons from outlying batteries marched toward Foshan by way of Nicheng and through Xiaoguan and Sanyuanli. Outraged villagers rallied militia from the surrounding townships and ambushed them on every side; over two hundred British troops were killed, and their commander Bremer was slain along with other officers.

sentences.zh: 義律馳援，復被圍。

translations.literal: Elliot rushed troops to rescue, and was again surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot hurried reinforcements to the scene and was surrounded in turn.

sentences.zh: 亟遣人突出告急於廣州知府余葆純，葆純馳往解散，翼義律出圍登舟免。

translations.literal: Urgently he sent someone to break out and report urgency to Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun; Baochun galloped there to disperse them, hoping Elliot could break out of the encirclement and board ships to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot sent a messenger through the lines to beg Guangzhou prefect Yu Baochun for help. Yu rode out and dispersed the crowd so Elliot could reach his boats and escape.

sentences.zh: 時三山村民亦擊殺英兵百餘。

translations.literal: At the time Sanshan village residents also struck and killed more than a hundred British soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time villagers at Sanshan killed more than a hundred British troops.

sentences.zh: 佛山義勇圍攻英民於龜岡砲臺，殲英兵數十，又擊破應援之杉板船。

translations.literal: Foshan righteous braves besieged English people at Guigang battery, annihilating several tens of British soldiers, and again smashed the supporting sampan boats.
translations.idiomatic: Foshan militia besieged British troops at Guigang battery, killing dozens and destroying the sampans sent to their relief.

sentences.zh: 新安亦以火攻毀其大兵船一，餘船遁。

translations.literal: Xin'an also used fire attack to destroy one of their large warships; the remaining ships fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Xin'an a fire attack destroyed one large British warship and the rest of the squadron withdrew.

sentences.zh: 義律牒總督示諭，眾始解散。

translations.literal: Elliot sent a document to the governor-general to issue proclamation, and the crowds then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot asked the governor-general to issue a proclamation, after which the militia stood down.

sentences.zh: 義律受挫，久之，始變計入閩，攻廈門，再陷。

translations.literal: Elliot, having suffered setbacks, after a long time at last changed plans and entered Fujian, attacking Xiamen, which again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by these defeats, Elliot eventually shifted operations to Fujian, captured Xiamen again, and pressed northward.

sentences.zh: 復統兵攻定海，總兵葛雲飛等戰沒。

translations.literal: He again led troops to attack Dinghai; Regional Commander Ge Yunfei and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He renewed the assault on Dinghai, where regional commander Ge Yunfei and other officers were killed.

sentences.zh: 裕謙以所部兵赴鎮海，方至，而英人自蛟門島來攻。

translations.literal: Yu Qian with his troops went to Zhenhai; they had just arrived when the British from Jiaomen Island came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian marched to Zhenhai with his force, but the British attacked from Jiaomen Island as soon as he arrived.

sentences.zh: 時鎮海防兵僅四千，提督余步雲與總兵謝朝恩各領其半。

translations.literal: At the time Zhenhai defensive troops were only four thousand; Commander Yu Buyun and Regional Commander Xie Chao'en each led half.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhai's garrison numbered only four thousand men, split between commander Yu Buyun and regional commander Xie Chao'en.

sentences.zh: 步雲違裕謙節制，不戰先走。

translations.literal: Bu Yun violated Yu Qian's command and control, not fighting but fleeing first.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Yun disobeyed Yu Qian's orders and fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 英遂據招寶山，俯攻鎮海，陷之。

translations.literal: The English then occupied Zhaobaoshan, looking down to attack Zhenhai, which fell.
translations.idiomatic: The British seized Zhaobaoshan, shelled Zhenhai from the heights, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 裕謙赴水死，謝朝恩亦戰歿。

translations.literal: Yu Qian went into the water and died; Xie Chao'en also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian drowned himself; Xie Chao'en also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 英人乘勝據寧波。

translations.literal: The English, riding victory, occupied Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious, the British occupied Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 八月，英人攻雞籠，為臺灣道姚瑩所敗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the English attacked Jilong and were defeated by Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a British attack on Jilong was repulsed by Taiwan circuit intendant Yao Ying.

sentences.zh: 九月，命大學士宗室奕經為揚威將軍，侍郎文蔚、副都統特依順為參贊大臣，赴浙，以怡良為欽差大臣，赴閩，會辦軍務。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Grand Secretary the clansman Yijing was ordered as Campaigning-General, Vice Minister Wen Wei and Vice Banner Commander Te Yishun as Advisory Grand Ministers, going to Zhejiang; Yiliang as Imperial Commissioner went to Fujian to jointly handle military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the imperial clansman Yijing was named Campaigning General, with Vice Minister Wen Wei and banner vice commander Te Yishun as grand commissioners for Zhejiang, while Yiliang was sent as imperial commissioner to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春正月，大兵進次紹興，將軍、參贊定議同日分襲寧波、鎮海。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-second year, the great army advanced and halted at Shaoxing; the general and advisory ministers fixed a plan to attack Ningbo and Zhenhai on the same day by divided assault.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, year 22, the main force encamped at Shaoxing. Yijing and his commissioners resolved to strike Ningbo and Zhenhai simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 豫泄師期，及戰，官軍多損失。

translations.literal: The campaign date was leaked in advance; when battle came, government troops suffered many losses.
translations.idiomatic: The attack schedule leaked beforehand, and government forces took heavy casualties when the assault was launched.

sentences.zh: 是月，姚瑩復敗英人于大安。

translations.literal: In that month, Yao Ying again defeated the English at Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Yao Ying again defeated the British at Da'an.

sentences.zh: 二月，英人攻慈谿營，金華協副將硃貴及其子武生昭南、督糧官即用知縣顏履敬死之。

translations.literal: In the second month, the English attacked the Cixi camp; Jinhua Assistant Regional Commander Zhu Gui and his son Military Student Zhu Zhaonan, and Grain Supervisor Acting Magistrate Yan Lüjing died therein.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the British attacked the camp at Cixi. Jinhua assistant regional commander Zhu Gui, his son the military licentiate Zhu Zhaonan, and acting magistrate Yan Lüjing, who oversaw grain supplies, were all killed.

sentences.zh: 是月，起用伊里布。

translations.literal: In that month, Yilibu was reappointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yilibu was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 先是伊里布解任，並逮其家人張喜入都遣戍。

translations.literal: Earlier Yilibu had been removed from office, and his household retainer Zhang Xi was also seized and sent to the capital for banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yilibu had earlier been dismissed, and his servant Zhang Xi was arrested and exiled to the capital with his household.

sentences.zh: 至是，浙撫劉韻琦請起用，報可。

translations.literal: At this point Zhejiang Governor Liu Yunqi requested his reappointment, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang governor Liu Yunqi now petitioned for his reinstatement, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 旋以耆英為杭州將軍，命臺灣設防。

translations.literal: Soon Qiying was made Hangzhou General, and an order was issued to fortify Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying was shortly appointed general at Hangzhou, and Taiwan's defenses were ordered strengthened.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，英人犯乍浦，副都統長喜、同知韋逢甲等戰死。

translations.literal: In the fourth summer month, the English violated Zhapu; Vice Banner Commander Chang Xi, Subprefect Wei Fengjia, and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month the British attacked Zhapu. Vice banner commander Chang Xi, subprefect Wei Fengjia, and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 時伊里布已來浙，即命家人張喜見英酋，告以撫事有成，令先退至大洋，即還所俘英人。

translations.literal: At the time Yilibu had already come to Zhejiang; he immediately ordered his household retainer Zhang Xi to see the English chieftain, telling him pacification matters were settled, ordering them first to withdraw to the open ocean, and then returning the captured English.
translations.idiomatic: Yilibu had by then reached Zhejiang. He sent his servant Zhang Xi to the British commander to say peace was assured, asked the fleet to withdraw to open water, and released the British prisoners.

sentences.zh: 英人如約，遂以收復乍浦奏聞。

translations.literal: The English kept the agreement; thereupon they memorialized reporting recovery of Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: The British complied, and the court was memorialized that Zhapu had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 英人連陷寶山、上海，江南提督陳化成等死之，遂犯松江，陷鎮江，殺副都統海齡。

translations.literal: The English in succession fell Baoshan and Shanghai; Jiangnan Commander Chen Huacheng and others died therein; they then violated Songjiang, fell Zhenjiang, and killed Vice Banner Commander Hai Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The British took Baoshan and Shanghai in succession; Jiangnan commander Chen Huacheng and others were killed. They then overran Songjiang, captured Zhenjiang, and killed vice banner commander Hai Ling.

sentences.zh: 淮揚鹽商懼甚，賂英師乞免。

translations.literal: Huai-Yang salt merchants were greatly afraid and bribed the English army begging exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified Huai-Yang salt merchants bribed the British fleet to spare their region.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，犯江寧。

translations.literal: In the seventh autumn month, they violated Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month they advanced on Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 英火輪兵船八十餘艘溯江上，自觀音門至下關。

translations.literal: More than eighty English steam warships went upriver from Guanyin Gate to Xiaguan.
translations.idiomatic: More than eighty British steam warships steamed up the Yangzi from Guanyin Gate to Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 時耆英方自浙啟行，伊里布亦奉詔自浙馳至，遣張喜詣英船道意。

translations.literal: At the time Qiying had just set out from Zhejiang; Yilibu also, by imperial edict, rushed from Zhejiang to arrive, and sent Zhang Xi to the English ships to convey intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying was just leaving Zhejiang when Yilibu, summoned by edict, hurried to Nanjing and sent Zhang Xi to the British fleet to open talks.

sentences.zh: 英人要求各款：一，索煙價、商欠、兵費銀二千一百萬；

translations.literal: The English demanded each item: first, demand opium indemnity, merchants' debts, and military expenses totaling 21 million taels of silver;
translations.idiomatic: Britain's demands ran as follows: first, twenty-one million taels in indemnity for opium, merchant debts, and war costs;

sentences.zh: 一，索香港為市埠，並通商廣州、福州、廈門、寧波、上海五口；

translations.literal: second, demand Hong Kong as a trading port, and open trade at Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai five ports;
translations.idiomatic: second, cession of Hong Kong as a treaty port and trade at Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai;

sentences.zh: 一，英官與中國官用敵體禮；

translations.literal: third, English officials and Chinese officials to use equal-body ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: third, diplomatic equality between British and Chinese officials;

sentences.zh: 餘則劃抵關稅、釋放漢奸等款，末請鈐用國寶。

translations.literal: the remainder then covered offsetting customs duties, releasing Han traitors, and other items; at the end they requested impressing the national seal.
translations.idiomatic: further clauses covered customs offsets, release of Chinese collaborators, and similar points, ending with a demand that the national seal be affixed.

sentences.zh: 會耆英至，按款稍駮詰。

translations.literal: When Qiying arrived, according to each item he slightly refuted and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiying arrived he raised modest objections to several clauses.

sentences.zh: 英突張紅旗，揚言今日如不定議，詰朝攻城，遂即夜覆書，一如所言。

translations.literal: The English suddenly raised a red flag, declaring that if terms were not fixed today, the city would be attacked tomorrow morning; they then that night returned a letter, exactly as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The British hoisted a red flag and warned that unless terms were settled that day they would assault the city at dawn. That night they sent back a written reply accepting exactly what had been demanded.

sentences.zh: 翼日，遣侍衛咸齡、布政司黃恩彤、寧紹臺道鹿澤長往告各款已代請，俟批回即定約。

translations.literal: The next day, they sent Attendant Xian Ling, Provincial Administration Commissioner Huang Entong, and Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit Intendant Lu Zechang to report each item had been memorialized on their behalf, awaiting imperial approval before fixing the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Attendant Xian Ling, provincial administration commissioner Huang Entong, and Ning-Shao-Tai circuit intendant Lu Zechang informed the British that every clause had been submitted for imperial approval and the treaty would be signed once the response arrived.

sentences.zh: 奏上，許之。

translations.literal: The memorial went up and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne and was approved.

sentences.zh: 時耆英、伊里布、牛鑒以將修好，遣張喜等約期相見。

translations.literal: At the time Qiying, Yilibu, and Niu Jian, because they were about to conclude peace, sent Zhang Xi and others to arrange a date to meet.
translations.idiomatic: With peace imminent, Qiying, Yilibu, and Niu Jian sent Zhang Xi and others to arrange a meeting.

sentences.zh: 馬利遜請以本國平行禮見。

translations.literal: Morrison requested to be received with his nation's parallel ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Morrison asked that the British be received with the ceremonial equality of their own country.

sentences.zh: 耆英等遂詣英舟，與璞鼎查等用舉手加額禮訂約，復親具牛酒犒師，畫諾於靜海寺，是為白門條約。

translations.literal: Qiying and others then went to the English ships and with Pottinger and others used the raised-hand-to-forehead ceremony to fix the treaty, again personally prepared oxen and wine to console the army, and initialed at Jinghai Temple—this was the Treaty of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying and his party went aboard the British ships, exchanged salutes with Pottinger and his staff, feasted the fleet, and signed the agreement at Jinghai Temple—the Treaty of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 自此煙禁遂大開矣。

translations.literal: From this the opium prohibition was greatly opened.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the ban on opium was effectively abandoned.

sentences.zh: 而英猶以臺灣殺英俘，為總兵達洪阿、兵備道姚瑩罪來詰，不得已，罷之。

translations.literal: Yet the English still, because Taiwan killed English captives, came to charge Regional Commander Da Hong'a and Military Preparedness Commissioner Yao Ying with guilt; having no alternative, they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Britain still demanded punishment for the execution of prisoners in Taiwan and blamed regional commander Da Hong'a and circuit intendant Yao Ying, who were dismissed under pressure.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以伊里布為欽差大臣，赴廣東督辦通商事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yilibu was made Imperial Commissioner, going to Guangdong to supervise and handle commercial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yilibu was appointed imperial commissioner to oversee trade in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十三年夏，伊里布卒，詔耆英往代。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-third year, Yilibu died; an edict ordered Qiying to go and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 23 Yilibu died, and Qiying was ordered to take his place.

sentences.zh: 先許英廣州通市。

translations.literal: Earlier permission had been given for the English to trade at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou trade for Britain had already been authorized.

sentences.zh: 初，英粵東互市章程，各國皆就彼掛號始輸稅。

translations.literal: Initially, under the English Guangdong mutual-trade regulations, every nation had to register with them before paying tax.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original Guangdong trade regulations, other nations had to register through Britain before paying duties.

sentences.zh: 法人、美人皆言「我非英屬」，不肯從，遂許法、美二國互市皆如英例。

translations.literal: French and Americans all said "we are not English subjects" and would not comply; thereupon France and America were both permitted mutual trade on the English model.
translations.idiomatic: French and American merchants insisted they were not British subjects and refused; France and the United States were then allowed the same trading terms as Britain.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，英人築福州烏石山，英領事官見浙閩總督劉韻珂，請立商埠，欲於會城內外自南臺至烏石山造洋樓，阻之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the English built on Fuzhou's Wushi Hill; the English consular officer saw Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Liu Yunke, requesting establishment of a trading port, wishing from within and without the provincial city from Nantai to Wushi Hill to build foreign buildings—this was obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 the British began construction on Fuzhou's Wushi Hill. The consul asked Governor-General Liu Yunke of Zhejiang and Fujian for a commercial settlement and sought to erect foreign buildings from Nantai to Wushi Hill inside and outside the walled city; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 值交還欠款，照江寧約，已付甲辰年銀二百五十萬，應將舟山、鼓浪嶼退還中國。

translations.literal: It happened that returning outstanding debt, according to the Nanjing treaty, had already paid 2.5 million taels of the Jiachen year; Zhoushan and Gulangyu should be returned to China.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Nanjing treaty outstanding payments were being settled; 2.5 million taels for the Jiachen year had been paid, and Zhoushan with Gulangyu were due to be returned to China.

sentences.zh: 英公使藉不許福州城內建樓事，不與交還。

translations.literal: The English minister, borrowing the matter of not permitting buildings inside Fuzhou city, would not hand them back.
translations.idiomatic: The British minister refused to return the islands, citing the refusal to allow construction inside Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 屢經辯論，始允退還鼓浪嶼，然執在彼建屋如故。

translations.literal: After repeated debate, he at last permitted return of Gulangyu, yet insisted on building houses there as before.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged argument he agreed to return Gulangyu but insisted on keeping the structures already built.

sentences.zh: 福州既得請，遂冀入居廣州城。

translations.literal: Fuzhou having obtained what was requested, they then hoped to enter and dwell in Guangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Having secured their points at Fuzhou, the British sought the right to reside inside Guangzhou's walls.

sentences.zh: 廣州民憤阻，揭帖議劫十三洋行，英酋逸去，入城之議遂不行。

translations.literal: Guangzhou residents angrily obstructed; posted placards discussed seizing the thirteen foreign factories; the English chieftain fled, and the proposal to enter the city thus did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese public opinion blocked the move; placards called for attacking the Thirteen Factories; the British chief fled, and the entry plan collapsed.

sentences.zh: 二十六年秋七月，英人還舟山。

translations.literal: In the seventh autumn month of the twenty-sixth year, the English returned Zhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, year 26, the British returned Zhoushan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，請與西藏定界通商，以非條約所載，不許。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, they requested fixing borders and trade with Tibet; because it was not recorded in the treaty, it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they asked to delimit borders and open trade with Tibet; the court refused because the treaty made no such provision.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，英酋文翰復請入廣州城互市，總督徐廣縉拒之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the English chief Wenhan again requested entering Guangzhou city to trade; Governor-General Xu Guangjin refused.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 British commissioner Wenhan again demanded entry into Guangzhou for trade; Governor-General Xu Guangjin refused.

sentences.zh: 越日，英舟闖入省河，廣縉單舸往諭，省河兩岸義勇呼聲震天。

translations.literal: The next day, English boats forced entry into the provincial river; Guangjin went alone in a small boat to instruct them, while on both banks of the provincial river righteous braves' shouts shook heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The next day British vessels forced their way up the provincial channel. Xu went out alone in a skiff to parley while militia on both banks roared their defiance.

sentences.zh: 文翰請仍修舊好，不復言入城事。

translations.literal: Wenhan requested still to repair the old good relations and no longer spoke of entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhan asked to restore friendly relations and dropped the demand to enter the city.

sentences.zh: 六年秋九月，英人巴夏里致書葉名琛，請循江寧舊約入城，不省。

translations.literal: In the ninth autumn month of the sixth year, the Englishman Parkes sent a letter to Ye Mingchen, requesting according to the old Nanjing treaty to enter the city; he did not review it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, year 6, Harry Parkes wrote to Ye Mingchen asking entry to the city under the Nanjing treaty; Ye ignored the letter.

sentences.zh: 英人攻粵城，不克逞，復請釋甲入見，亦不許。

translations.literal: The English attacked Guangzhou city, could not succeed in their aim, again requested disarming to enter and be received in audience, and this too was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: British forces attacked Canton without success, then asked to lay down arms for an audience; that too was refused.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，攻虎門橫檔各砲臺，又為廣州義勇所卻，乃馳告其國。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, they attacked Humen Hengdang and other batteries, and were again repelled by Guangzhou righteous braves; they then galloped to report to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month they assaulted the Humen and Hengdang batteries but were driven off again by Canton militia, then hurried word home for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 於是簡其伯爵額爾金來華，擬由粵入都，先將火輪兵船分泊澳門、香港以俟。

translations.literal: Thereupon they selected their Earl Elgin to come to China, planning to enter the capital from Guangdong, first dispersing steam war vessels to anchor at Macao and Hong Kong to await.
translations.idiomatic: The crown then dispatched Earl Elgin to China, intending to reach the capital via Canton while steam men-of-war took station at Macao and Hong Kong to await his orders.

sentences.zh: 額爾金至粵，初謀入城，不可。

translations.literal: Elgin reached Guangdong; at first he plotted entering the city—this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Elgin reached Canton and at once pressed to enter the walled city, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 與水師提督、領事等議款，牒粵中官吏，俟其復書定進止，名琛置不答。

translations.literal: With the naval commander-in-chief, consul, and others he discussed terms, sent documents to Guangdong officials, awaited their reply to fix advance or halt; Mingchen placed it aside and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He negotiated terms with the admiral and consuls and notified Canton officials that he would await their reply before acting; Ye Mingchen ignored the messages entirely.

sentences.zh: 七年冬十二月，英人遂合法、美、俄攻城，城陷，執名琛去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth winter month of the seventh year, the English thereupon joined France, America, and Russia in attacking the city; the city fell, and they seized Mingchen and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, year 7, British forces allied with France, the United States, and Russia to storm the city; Canton fell and Ye Mingchen was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 因歸罪粵中官吏，上書大學士裕誠求達。

translations.literal: Thereupon blaming Guangdong officials, he sent up a memorial to Grand Secretary Yucheng requesting conveyance.
translations.idiomatic: Elgin blamed the Canton authorities and memorialized Grand Secretary Yucheng to relay his grievances to the throne.

sentences.zh: 裕誠覆書，令赴粵與新命粵督黃宗漢商辦，不省。

translations.literal: Yucheng replied by letter, ordering him to go to Guangdong and consult with the newly appointed Guangdong governor Huang Zonghan; he did not review it.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng answered that he should return to Canton and treat with the new governor, Huang Zonghan; Elgin took no notice.

sentences.zh: 八年夏四月，聯兵犯大沽，連陷前路砲臺。

translations.literal: In the fourth summer month of the eighth year, the allied armies violated Dagukou, continuously seizing the forward batteries.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, year 8, allied fleets struck the Dagu forts and captured the outer batteries in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝命科爾沁親王僧格林沁率師赴天津防剿，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Prince Sengge Rinchen of Khorchin to lead troops to Tianjin for defense and suppression; the capital was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Sengge Rinchen of Khorchin to march on Tianjin with an army, and Beijing was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 帝命大學士桂良、吏部尚書花沙納赴天津查辦，復起用耆英偕往。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister of Personnel Huashana to proceed to Tianjin to investigate and handle matters, and again raised and employed Qiying to go together.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Grand Secretaries Guiliang and Huashana, Minister of Personnel, to Tianjin to conduct talks, reappointing the veteran negotiator Qiying to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 耆英至，往謁英使，不得見，擅自回京，賜自盡。

translations.literal: Qiying arrived, went to call on the English envoy, could not obtain an audience, on his own authority returned to the capital, and was bestowed death by suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying called on the British envoy but was refused an audience; he returned to Beijing without authorization and was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 英有里國太者，嘉應州人也，世仰食外洋，隨英公使額爾金為行營參贊。

translations.literal: Among the English there was one Li Guotai, a man of Jiaying prefecture, whose family for generations depended on food from foreign seas; he followed the English minister Elgin as camp counsellor of the marching headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Among Elgin's staff was Horatio Nelson Lay, a native of Jiaying prefecture whose family had long lived on foreign employ; he served the envoy as camp adviser.

sentences.zh: 聞桂良至，即持所定新議五十六條，要桂良允許，桂良辭之。

translations.literal: Hearing Guiliang had arrived, he immediately held the fifty-six articles of the newly fixed agreement, demanding Guiliang permit them; Guiliang declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiliang arrived, Lay pressed the fifty-six draft articles and demanded immediate acceptance; Guiliang refused.

sentences.zh: 津民憤，與英人鬥，擒里國太將殺之。

translations.literal: Tianjin people were inflamed; they fought with the English, seized Li Guotai and were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin crowds, enraged, clashed with the British and seized Lay, nearly executing him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 桂良、譚廷襄恐誤撫局，亟遣人釋里國太，送回舟。

translations.literal: Guiliang and Tan Tingxiang feared spoiling the pacification situation, urgently sent men to release Li Guotai and return him to the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the negotiations would collapse, Guiliang and Tan Tingxiang hurriedly had Lay released and sent back to his ship.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣交章請罷撫議，以疆事棘，不得已，始命桂良等與定和約五十六款。

translations.literal: At the time court ministers submitted memorials one after another requesting cessation of pacification talks; because frontier affairs were thorny, having no alternative, they then ordered Guiliang and others to fix the peace treaty in fifty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: Officials bombarded the throne with pleas to abandon talks, but with the frontier crisis acute the court had no choice and finally ordered Guiliang to sign the fifty-six-article treaty.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣桂良、花沙納巡視江蘇，籌議諸國通商稅則。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, they dispatched Guiliang and Huashana to inspect Jiangsu and deliberate the commercial-tax rules for the various states.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Guiliang and Huashana were sent to tour Jiangsu and draft a uniform tariff for foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，定通商稅則。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, the commercial-tax rules were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth winter month the tariff schedule was settled.

sentences.zh: 時英人以條約許增設長江海口商埠，欲先察看沿江形勢。

translations.literal: At the time the English, because the treaty permitted adding Yangtze river-mouth commercial ports, wished first to reconnoitre conditions along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The treaty allowed new treaty ports on the Yangtze, and the British now wanted to reconnoiter the river before opening them.

sentences.zh: 定約後，即遣水師、領事以輪船入江，溯流至漢口，逾月而返。
